meta.title: Writing fails
meta.description: A collection of misreadings caused by direction, layout, letterforms, typos, wording, unfamiliar scripts or translation.

hero.tagline: Words can mean something else when read in the wrong direction—or the wrong order.

empty: No entries found. Try another search or filter.

land.description: 임야, 대지, 상가 (forest land, building land, shops) becomes 상대임 가지야—an apparent nonsense phrase.
land.alt: A Korean property sign with text arranged in vertical columns

poem.description: A lesson on poverty and study turns into “eat people, eat people.”
poem.alt: A Chinese text laid out in vertical columns

sign.description: Four soups ending in 탕 (tang) become 탕탕탕탕—the sound of gunshots.
sign.alt: A Korean sign whose layout invites an unintended reading

udon.description: うどん・そば (udon and soba) becomes the nonsensical そどうばん.
udon.alt: A photographed udon and soba shop sign

converter.description: “HD video converter” becomes “erotic video converter” when HD resembles エロ.
converter.alt: The photographed HD video converter packaging

meat.description: 肉のこーべや (Kobeya Meat) becomes “this meat is bad.”
meat.alt: A red butcher shop sign reading 肉のこーべや

menu.description: Read down, the endings of menu items become a rhythmic string of syllables.
menu.alt: A close-up of repeated characters on a restaurant menu

warning.description: A warning that the rooftop observation deck is slippery reads like a strange poem down the columns.
warning.alt: A Japanese warning sign arranged in short horizontal rows

pillow.description: スゴイまくら (“amazing pillow”) becomes three puzzling pairs when each banner is read down.
pillow.alt: Three banners spelling スゴイまくら

drinks.description: The drink list is set in rows; read down the third column, the kana spell コロン, “colon.”
drinks.alt: A yellow handwritten drinks menu with three rows of large red kana

lift.description: 荷物リフト, コンベヤ and 投入リフト run down the sign in columns; read across, the kana line up as リベリ and フヤフ.
lift.alt: A tall white station sign with columns of brushed black lettering and one red column

dental.description: Four treatments run left to right; the third column spells 修正牙口, “fix your teeth.” 牙口好, “good teeth,” goes with a hearty appetite.
dental.alt: A blue dental clinic sign listing four treatments in white rows

banner.description: The columns read right to left: 指望传销致富、生活没有出路, a warning against pyramid schemes. Left to right they become 生活没有出路、指望传销致富—the warning turns into an invitation.
banner.alt: A blue police banner with two vertical columns of white Chinese characters

inari.description: The panels step down from the right and read right to left: すべての電車が稲荷駅に停車します, “all trains stop at Inari Station.” Read left to right, they become すまし車停…
inari.alt: Brown panels of white Japanese characters stepping down a station wall from right to left

yoyaku.description: The panels read ご予約 along the top and 受付中 along the bottom; read down each panel instead and they become ご受予付約中.
yoyaku.alt: Three red panels on a fence, each stacked with two white characters

slogans.description: The poster sets 人民相信党 above 没有好下场; read as one sentence, the lines say the people trust the Party—and come to no good end.
slogans.alt: A red renovation wrap with a poster reading 人民相信党 above 没有好下场

sign-order.description: The stall meant 没有科技，都是手艺—no tech, all craft. The panels went up with 科技 and 手艺 the wrong way round, so the sign promises the opposite; the shop went viral anyway.
sign-order.alt: A wooden restaurant sign reading 没有手艺，都是科技 under its name

rumeso.description: A tea shop's ラーメン banner was flipped and hung sideways about a decade ago; seen from the back the mirrored kana read ルーメソ, and the shop kept it that way.
rumeso.alt: A pink banner with large white kana hung sideways under a shop roof

billboard.description: 999 感冒灵 hung its billboard upside down for exam season: the logo reads 666, the students' shorthand for doing brilliantly.
billboard.alt: A green bus-stop billboard mounted upside down, its 999 logo reading 666

noren.description: The noren at the eel restaurant 小川菊 sets うなぎ right to left; read left to right, the same kana spell ぎなう.
noren.alt: A navy noren with 小川菊 in white at the left and the kana ぎなう across it

toraya.description: The confectioner とらや hangs its noren with the name set right to left; read left to right, the kana spell やらと.
toraya.alt: A white noren across a shop front with the kana やらと in black

florist.description: The florist's sign sets ハナ right to left, so the kana read ナハ—while FLORIST above it runs the ordinary way.
florist.alt: A green hanging sign reading FLORIST above the kana ナハ and a right-to-left phone line

yamaki.description: The old sign sets 山基産業株式会社 right to left; read left to right it opens 社会式, and the company name runs backwards.
yamaki.alt: A dark wooden shop sign reading 社会式株業産基山 above older wooden signs

tenpura.description: The tempura shop's noren sets 天婦羅 right to left; read left to right, the characters become 羅婦天.
tenpura.alt: A dark noren reading 羅婦天 in white above a wooden shop front

yuujin.description: The notice sets its columns left to right, the opposite of vertical Japanese, so right-to-left readers get the lines backwards—and 有人レジ, the staffed register, is typed 友人レジ.
yuujin.alt: A handwritten notice in three vertical columns

nhyo.description: Weathering ate parts of the ショッパーズ sign and left ンョ゛ハー; the rooftop sign above still spells the shop's name.
nhyo.alt: A supermarket facade with a weathered sign reading ンョ゛ハー and an intact rooftop sign

kaoliang.description: The old label sets 特級高粱酒 right to left, so a left-to-right reader gets 酒粱高級特; Kinmen's labels switched direction around 1980.
kaoliang.alt: An old Kinmen Kaoliang bottle whose red label text runs right to left

karamen.description: The shop is called ちからラーメン, but the sign draws 力 as カ and leaves ちから in tiny furigana—so passersby read “colour ramen.”
karamen.alt: A yellow shop sign reading カラーメン with tiny ちから furigana above the first character

graduation.description: The graduation board meant 前途亦灿灿, “the future shines,” but printed 烂烂, so it wishes the class a rotten future instead.
graduation.alt: A graduation board reading 人生路漫 前途亦烂烂, with 烂烂 circled in red

poster-711.description: The poster meant 夯爆了, slang for “a hit,” but printed 劣爆了, “terrible,” so the advert insulted the ice cream it was selling.
poster-711.alt: A 7-Eleven poster reading 听劝上架啦，劣爆了 above pictures of ice cream

mirrored-gate.description: The estate stencil was sprayed from the wrong side, mirroring every stroke of 金秋小区; repainting kept the error alive for twenty years.
mirrored-gate.alt: A residential gate whose four characters 金秋小区 are painted with mirrored strokes

kitasenju.description: The renewed board for 北千住 printed 干 in place of 千, so it reads 北干住 while the furigana below still says きたせんじゅ.
kitasenju.alt: A station board reading 北干住 with the furigana きたせんじゅ and Kita-senju underneath

wife.description: The shop meant Wi-Fi, but the board advertises a wife instead: wifeあります, charging OK.
wife.alt: A white board reading wifeあります 充電OK above a menu for beef tongue

mataichi.description: The parking sign belongs to うなぎの又一, but the shop name 又一 is drawn so that it reads as the katakana ヌー.
mataichi.alt: A parking sign for an eel restaurant whose name reads as the katakana ヌー

spouse.description: The evacuation sign in Minamisanriku renders スポーツ交流村 as Spouse Exchange Village, two letters short of a sports facility.
spouse.alt: A sign pairing スポーツ交流村 with the English line Spouse Exchange Village

summit.description: The trail sign says 山頂はこちら, “the summit is this way”; the machine translation underneath reads Click here for the summit, as if the mountain were a link.
summit.alt: A yellow arrow sign reading 山頂はこちら above the English line Click here for the summit

panda.description: The zoo asks visitors to view quietly; its Chinese line 静静請看 also reads as “please look, Jingjing”, turning the adverb into a panda’s name.
panda.alt: A panda poster reading お静かにご覧ください over Quiet Please and 静静請看

soldout.description: The board lists departure time, cars and doors; the 8:21 train’s door count reads Sold Out, the translation of 満席—the train is full, not on sale.
soldout.alt: A station board showing 8:21, 8Car and Sold Out in the door column

lunch.description: The banner advertises ランチ 1000円～; written in hiragana and caught by the wind, the ら bends into う, so lunch reads as うんち.
lunch.alt: A white banner in the wind reading うんち above a 0

rikei.description: A 野菜直売所 banner hung inside-out; from the back the mirrored characters read 理系直売所—“science department direct sales.”
rikei.alt: A green banner seen from the back whose mirrored characters read 理系直売所

irasshai.description: The same inside-out trick on a shop banner: いらっしゃいませ comes back as りさっしゃいまサ.
irasshai.alt: A red banner seen from the back whose mirrored kana read りさっしゃいまサ

shachi.description: A シャモ鍋 banner hung inside-out; from the back the mirrored characters read シャチ鍋, an orca hotpot instead of chicken.
shachi.alt: A white banner with シャチ鍋 and a photo of a hotpot, seen from the back

bonkhatsu.description: The festival-lantern banner 盆提灯, read from the back, becomes 盆髪城—a hair castle for the bon holiday.
bonkhatsu.alt: A beige banner whose mirrored characters read 盆髪城

usomasakoshi.description: The sweet-corn banner read from the wrong side: とうもろこし comes out as うそまさこし, which opens with “lie.”
usomasakoshi.alt: A corn banner seen from the back, its red kana reading うそまさこし

mad.description: A karaoke banner hung inside-out: the brand ＤＡＭ reads ＭＡＤ.
mad.alt: A red banner with MAD at the top, photographed from the back

ryuma.description: A Kochi banner for リョーマの休日 seen from the back: the mirrored kana read リューマの村日, a village day instead of a holiday.
ryuma.alt: A white Kochi banner seen from the back, its kana reading リューマの村日

huixiang.description: The lit sign says 徽乡宴府; the wooden plaque below spells it 微乡宴府, minus the 徽’s top. The shop calls the error deliberate.
huixiang.alt: A restaurant with 徽乡宴府 on the lit sign and 微乡宴府 on the wooden plaque below

polyu.description: The Mid-Autumn banner quotes Su Shi’s 千里共嬋娟; converted from simplified to traditional without proofreading, 里 came out as 裡, “inside.”
polyu.alt: A purple banner reading 但願人長久，千裡共嬋娟

haitang.description: The Wujiang shop sells 海棠糕, the begonia-shaped cake; its sign sets 堂 for 棠, and locals argue over whether the slip is carelessness or marketing.
haitang.alt: A snack shop sign reading 梅花糕 海堂糕 in yellow characters on teal

disncy.description: A temporary Hong Kong road sign sends drivers to Disncy and Tung Chun, a letter short in both names.
disncy.alt: A yellow temporary road sign listing Tung Chun and Disncy

human.description: A new Shanghai metro station letters 呼玛路 as Human Road, the input method finishing the word, and 富锦路 as Fujin Poad.
human.alt: A metro sign with 呼玛路 above Human Road, the n circled in red

friedfish.description: The park bans 炸鱼, fishing with explosives; the translation takes 炸 as “fried” and outlaws fried fish instead.
friedfish.alt: A park notice board whose 禁止炸鱼 sign is translated No Fried Fish

menu-rhythm.description: A Yau Ma Tei cha chaan teng writes its menu by sound: 黑椒雞扒飯 comes out 克召雞扒反, legible only if you say it aloud in Cantonese.
menu-rhythm.alt: A handwritten cha chaan teng menu whose items are spelled by sound

nuclear.description: The boat ticket board caps 核載12人, certified for twelve passengers; the English renders 核載 as “nuclear loading”, as if the boat ran on a reactor.
nuclear.alt: A ticket board printing 核载12人 and the English nuclear loading 12 people

carefully.description: A toilet doorway in Zhaoyu’s old town warns 小心碰头, mind your head; the English renders it word for word as “Carefully Meet”.
carefully.alt: A small sign reading 小心碰头 above the English Carefully Meet

lionforest.description: A Suzhou lamp-post sign gives 平江路 the English name of 狮子林, the garden next door, and shortens it to THE LION FOREST GARD.
lionforest.alt: A brown lamp-post sign labelling 平江路 as THE LION FOREST GARD

slip.description: The tile warns 小心地滑, “caution: slippery floor”; read word by word, 地 becomes the adverb and the sign orders you to slip carefully.
slip.alt: A green sign reading 小心地滑 above Slip carefully

hottopic.description: The café board writes ホットドック, a kana short of ホットドッグ, and under it offers “Hot topic”—neither a hot dog nor a subject.
hottopic.alt: A chalkboard reading ホットドック above Hot topic

ganmo.description: The buffet labels がんも煮物, simmered ganmo tofu; the English reads “Boiled cancer”, as if がん had been taken for 癌.
ganmo.alt: A buffet card reading がんも煮物 above Boiled cancer

emu.description: A toilet on the Xi’an–Chengdu train asks passengers not to flush while passing another 动车; the abbreviation EMU turns the train into an emu.
emu.alt: A train toilet sign reading 与动车交汇时请勿冲水 above NO FLUSHING WHILE MEETING EMU

civil.description: The board asks drivers to keep the route 文明, civilised; the English orders them to “SET UP THE CIVILIZATION PASSAGE” instead.
civil.alt: A blue highway board reading 建文明通道 above SET UP THE CIVILIZATION PASSAGE

nocandy.description: The supermarket labels its 无糖食品专架, the sugar-free food shelf, “There be no candy food”—a sentence about absence instead of a section name.
nocandy.alt: A yellow supermarket sign reading 无糖食品专架 above There be no candy food

levelgap.description: At a Shanghai ferry dock, 注意高低空档, mind the step between boat and shore, becomes the memo “NOTE THAT THE LEVEL OF GAP”.
levelgap.alt: A Shanghai ferry sign reading 注意高低空档 above NOTE THAT THE LEVEL OF GAP

climmbing.description: At the Tiantishan grottoes the sign says 请勿攀爬, do not climb; the English doubles the m and slips a b in: “No climmbing”.
climmbing.alt: A brown sign reading 请勿攀爬 above No climmbing

justdoti.description: A Taoyuan campaign billboard borrows the Nike line and prints the last two letters the wrong way round: “JUST DO TI”.
justdoti.alt: A campaign billboard with the large letters DO TI

shijuku.description: A JR Nishifunabashi sign lists 新宿 as “Shijuku”, one n short; the correction is a white sticker pasted over the missing letter.
shijuku.alt: A station sign reading 新宿 with the English Shijuku pasted over

yen.description: The sticker sheet prints ￥ signs; turned upside down, their strokes read as 夫, so the shop appears to stock husbands by the sheet.
yen.alt: A sheet of red stickers reading 夫, which are upside-down ￥ signs

zibo.description: A Zibo billboard drops the 未 from 关爱未成年人, “care for minors”, so the slogan asks the public to protect adults instead.
zibo.alt: A billboard whose circled line reads 关爱和保护成年人

henan-beijing.description: The 出口 374 board names 河北 and 南京, one per line. Read down the columns and the four characters become 河南 and 北京. The picture is an edit; the original sign is unknown.
henan-beijing.alt: A green 出口 374 highway sign showing 河北 over 南京, with an arrow below pointing up and to the right

tsutaya.description: A Kōchi card shop congratulated its winner as クソヘタ怪人石神; the handle is クセヘタ, and the swapped セ and ソ call him hopeless at the game.
tsutaya.alt: A correction post reading 誤:クソヘタ怪人石神 and 正:クセヘタ怪人石神

teabag.description: The tea chain’s bag seals read 打包在忙，吸管别忘; the line needs 再, “however busy packing gets”, so the typo turns a reminder into a status report.
teabag.alt: A tea-shop bag seal reading 打包在忙 吸管别忘

nowwa.description: A Nowwa Coffee light-box credits its ambassador as 帅气青年男性, “handsome young male”, in the slot where his name belongs.
nowwa.alt: A poster whose vertical title reads 帅气青年男性 beside the brand line

lamb.description: A Shanghai lamb restaurant prices its cuts at 19元（客）, per portion; 客 was typed 克, so the menu charges 19 yuan a gram—9,500 a jin.
lamb.alt: A menu pricing three lamb dishes at 19元（克）, circled in red

tuni.description: Shanghai Disney’s annual-pass booklet prints 迪士尼 as 迪土尼, putting 土 for 士, so the park’s name gains a “tu”.
tuni.alt: A Disneyland annual-pass line reading 上海迪士尼乐园 with an arrow at the 土

killfish.description: Daiso’s soil for medaka promised a comfortable environment “for killifish”; one i went missing, so the label sells a fish-killing substrate.
killfish.alt: A Daiso apology notice reading 誤:killfish 正:killifish

heelo.description: The wash label on Luckin’s Hello Kitty charm prints HELLO as HEELO; online the extra E turned the greeting into 喝喽, “drink up”.
heelo.alt: A blue wash label reading HEELO KITTY over luckin coffee

hayabue.description: A supporter’s rally board outside Matsudo Station prints 高市早苗 as 高市早笛—苗 swapped for 笛, turning the candidate into a flute.
hayabue.alt: A rally signboard reading 高市 早笛

meiwaku.description: A construction sign merges ご迷惑をおかけします and ご協力をお願いします into ご迷惑をお願いします—“please be inconvenienced”.
meiwaku.alt: A construction sign reading ご迷惑をお願いします above 原状回復工事を行っています
meiwaku.intended: ご迷惑をおかけします
meiwaku.misread: ご迷惑をお願いします

unchi.description: The pork-chop shop 豬排屋 lists 極上, 絶品中華 and 和風 lunches, but every ラ came out as う: 極上うンチ, 絶品中華うンチ and 和風うンチ.
unchi.alt: A red signboard reading 美味 豬排屋 with three lunch lines set as うンチ

noppo.description: Noppo-kun’s profile card gives his height as 10.5m. The unit should be centimetres, which makes the hamster more than ten metres tall.
noppo.alt: The shop’s notice comparing the card reading 10.5m with the corrected 10.5cm

imagry.description: The cup prints IMAGRY where the slogan needs IMAGERY; the missing E leaves a word that does not exist.
imagry.alt: A paper cup with the word IMAGRY boxed in red

yisi.description: A promotion notice praising a colleague’s 一絲不苟, meticulous, work prints 一絲不掛 instead—“stark naked”, one character away.
yisi.alt: A promotion notice with the phrase 處事一絲不掛 spotlighted

double-fight.description: The English menu renders 雙拼, a two-item combo, as “double fight”, and 腸粉, a rice-noodle roll, as “intestine powder”.
double-fight.alt: Menu boards pairing 蘿蔔生菜雙拼 with “Radish and lettuce double fight”

cold-is-self.description: お冷はセルフサービスです says the cold water is self-service; the English line makes it “cold is self”, as if the self were a temperature.
cold-is-self.alt: A sign reading お冷はセルフサービスです above “cold is self・冷是自己”

faan.description: The handwritten fast-food board ends every rice dish in 反, “reverse”, where 飯, rice, belongs, so curry pork slices become 咖喱肉片反.
faan.alt: A handwritten fast-food board listing 咖喱肉片反 and 雞反

guzhang.description: Told that a staff notice's 壞咗 was too colloquial, the manager rewrote it as 固障—the word for a fault is 故障.
guzhang.alt: A slip reading 固障 stuck to a shop counter

wuxian.description: A campaign billboard promised 你＋台北 就是無限 but went up as 就無是限, with 是 and 無 swapped, so the slogan stops parsing.
wuxian.alt: A campaign billboard reading 台北 就無是限, circled in red

gimpo.description: Gimpo Airport set its Korean terminal names in katakana, so 国際線 appears as ククチェソン—the hangul 국제선 spelled out in Japanese script.
gimpo.alt: An airport sign pairing 国际航线 ククチェソン with 국제선

britian.description: The brown tourist sign points to the ss Great Britain but prints it Great Britian, one letter short of the ship.
britian.alt: A brown road sign reading ss Great Britian

paulente.description: A Jersey road sign sends drivers to La Paulente; the coastal slipway it means is La Pulente.
paulente.alt: A Jersey road sign listing La Paulente

consejales.description: A municipal directory in Luque lists the councillors as CONSEJALES; the Spanish word is concejales, and the missing c is the story.
consejales.alt: A municipal directory with CONSEJALES circled in red

patick.description: A green street sign in Ottawa sends drivers to St. Patick Street; the R in Patrick never made it onto the plate.
patick.alt: A green Ottawa street sign reading Rue St. Patick Street
